Films | released = {{Film date|1951|12|14|df=y}} | runtime = 168 minutes | country = [[India]] | language = [[Hindustani language|Hindustani]] | music = [[Shankar–Jaikishan]] | budget = | gross = {{Estimation}} {{INR|15.6 crore}} }} [[File:Awaara (1951).webm|thumb|x150px|thumbtime=2:10:03|''Awaara'' (1951)]] '''''Awaara''''', also written '''''Awāra'''''{{#tag:ref|{{langx|hi|[[wikt:आवारा|आवारा]]}}, {{langx|ur|{{nastaliq|[[wikt:آوارہ|آوارہ]]}}|Āvārā}}|group=n|name=HindiUrdu}} and known overseas as '''''The Vagabond''''',{{Cite book |last=Malenbaum |first=Wilfred |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8i8EAAAAMAAJ |title=East and West in India's Development |date=1959 |publisher=[[MIT Center for International Studies]] |page=43 |language=en}} is a [[1951 in film|1951]] [[Cinema of India|Indian]] [[crime drama]] film, produced and directed by [[Raj Kapoor]], and written by [[Khwaja Ahmad Abbas]] and V.P. Sathe. It stars Raj Kapoor along with his real-life father [[Prithviraj Kapoor]], as well as [[Nargis]], [[Leela Chitnis]] and [[K. N. Singh]]. Other members of the [[Kapoor family]] make an appearance, including Raj's youngest brother [[Shashi Kapoor]], who plays the younger version of his character, and Prithiviraj's father Dewan Basheshwarnath Singh Kapoor, playing a cameo in his only film appearance. The film's music was composed by [[Shankar Jaikishan]]. The film expresses [[socialist]] themes, and blends [[Social problem film|social]] and [[reformist]] themes with the [[Crime film|crime]], [[romantic comedy]] and [[Musical film|musical]] [[melodrama]] genres.{{cite book |last1=Creekmur |first1=Corey K. |title=International Film Musical |date=2013 |publisher=[[Edinburgh University Press]] |isbn=978-0-7486-5430-7 |page=217 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gZJvAAAAQBAJ&pg=PT217}} The plot centers on the intertwining lives of a poor thief Raj (played by Raj Kapoor), the privileged Rita (played by Nargis), and Judge Raghunath (played by Prithviraj Kapoor) who is unaware that Raj is his son.
